detail.reference: There are $11!!=10395$ pairings. If $G$ starts the last word, its partner has 5 choices; the other four higher letters must pair with distinct lower letters, giving $5(6\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3)=1800$ pairings. Otherwise, the last word must be $FG$, giving $5!=120$ pairings. Thus the probability is $1920/10395=128/693$, so $m+n=\boxed{821}$.
